demo._all:
@id non-conformists
@layout cover

# Here’s to the crazy ones.

The ones who see things differently.

@narrative
  direction:
    notes: >-
      Begin as a quiet toast, then add warmth with the second sentence.
      Speak only the two script sentences. Do not read these notes, the scene,
      or the style brief aloud.
  entries: '{{ messages[0].quotes }}'
@id dcp-boring
@layout cover

# J:

I think DCP is kind of boring.

(sent handsfree from my second Tesla)

@narrative
  direction:
    style: Casual and offhand, like a voice text from a car.
    pacing: Natural conversational cadence; treat the parenthetical as a quiet send-status, not a punchline shout.
    notes: Keep “J” as a brief speaker tag, then the complaint, then the Tesla footer as an afterthought. Speak only the language of this script — never switch languages.
  entries: '{{ messages[1].quotes }}'
@id from-target
@layout cover

# From Target:

Dan, you owe us 100 compute credits, not to mention the compounding damage caused by implying to our customers that we would be giving away anything for free!

@narrative
  direction:
    style: Formal, clipped, and faintly indignant — a corporate complaint, not a toast.
    pacing: Even and pointed; let the free-giveaway clause land without shouting.
    notes: Read “From Target” as a sender line, then address Dan by name.
  entries: '{{ messages[2].quotes }}'
@id desjardins-fridge
@layout cover

# From Desjardin’s fridge:

Dan, your son is running out of milk! Be sure to bring some when you’re done.

@narrative
  direction:
    style: Flat, robotic smart-appliance voice. Even pitch, little warmth, slight Canadian English.
    pacing: Measured and slightly mechanical; do not rush the milk warning.
    accent: Canadian English.
    notes: >-
      Read “From Desjardin’s fridge” as a device sender line, then the warning to Dan.
      Stay in Canadian English only. Sound like a household robot, not a film narrator.
  entries: '{{ messages[3].quotes }}'

app.title: DCP Social Media Transcoder
app.tagline: Record in the browser. Select platforms. Transcode on DCP. Influence the world.

worker_invite.notes: Public GitHub Pages browser worker encoded by the account QR code (replaces dcp.live).

audience.notes: When Emulate audience is on, each DCP slice that arrives with no worker comment is considered for a unique catalog quote (Gemini WAV). The insert chance starts at chance_percent and rises as remaining empty slices shrink (remaining messages / remaining empty slices), reaching 100% once no spare slices remain, so the full catalog is placed by the end of the job with high probability. Messages are never reused in the same job. Playback of an earlier comment only skips a roll while spare slices remain.

vp9.name: VP9
vp9.notes: Preferred MediaRecorder video codec when supported

h264.name: H.264 / AVC
h264.notes: Cross-platform social upload master video codec

aac_lc.name: AAC-LC
aac_lc.notes: Cross-platform social upload master audio codec

cover.label: Fill (center crop)
cover.description: Scale to cover the target canvas, then center-crop. Prefer for feed and short-form masters.

contain.label: Fit (pad)
contain.description: Scale to fit inside the target canvas and pad. Prefer when the full frame must be preserved.

stretch.label: Stretch
stretch.description: Distorts to exact width×height. Avoid for social masters.

social_default.notes: Normalize browser VFR MediaRecorder timelines to 30 fps CFR.

input.timing: Potentially VFR; normalize to 30 fps CFR

dispatch.notes: Identical Meta feed/reels specs encode once and alias to every selected deliverable name.

bank.notes: Identity must be set before opening the teller connection (EHAVEIDENTITY is non-fatal). The queried account key may also be the identity. Request viewAccount with { address }, authorize with that account's PrivateKey or Keystore, then read payload.balance.

github.notes: Browser uploads via GitHub Contents API, dispatches the self-hosted runner test workflow, then pays for one DCP slice whose work function lists dcp-gh-runner/dcpGhRunner.js and ffmpeg-dcp-social-v2/ffmpeg-wasm.js in job.requires (packages ship with the job). The slice JIT-registers as a GitHub Actions runner, transcodes to li_feed MP4, then publishes via LinkedIn REST (when token + URN provided) or GitHub commit + post-to-linkedin workflow.

probe.label: Probe WebM
probe.description: Confirm VP8/VP9, dimensions, audio presence, and timing.

slice.label: Keyframe-aligned WebM slice
slice.description: Stream-copy independent WebM chunks at video keyframes (~3 s @ 30 fps).

encode.label: DCP encode
encode.description: One fleet slice per (chunk, unique format). Decode once per worker unit; emit H.264/AAC MPEG-TS.

assemble.label: Assemble + remux MP4
assemble.description: Ordered concat per format signature, then faststart MP4 remux. Independent signatures finalize concurrently.

x_feed.notes: X timeline 720p master for broadest playback

youtube.name: YouTube
youtube.notes: Bitrate-hungry; prefer native 16:9 and 9:16 without baked bars.

x.name: X (Twitter)
x.notes: 720p default for broadest playback; Premium 1080p is optional elsewhere.

_payload.notes: X timeline 720p master for broadest playback

instagram.name: Instagram
instagram.notes: Shares Meta feed/reels geometry with Facebook for encode dedupe.

facebook.name: Facebook
facebook.notes: Same Meta masters as Instagram; identical signatures encode once.

linkedin.name: LinkedIn
linkedin.notes: Ad-safe ≤30 fps masters for organic and sponsored reuse.
